title: Cold-Sear: A Fast, Dry-Heat Steak Sear Demonstration (Lan Lam, Techniquely)
summary: The video compares multiple steak-cooking philosophies, foregrounding a fast, low-mess method called cold-searing while also explaining traditional pan-sear, oven-finish, reverse-sear, and sous-vide approaches. Lan Lam contrasts the outcomes (edge-to-edge doneness with a rosy center vs. a gray ring) and details a step-by-step cold-sear process using a dry, hot non-stick skillet, a thick boneless steak, and careful heat management. Key practices include drying the surface, peppering before searing, avoiding pre-salt, heating to drive off surface moisture, flipping every two minutes to build multiple brown layers, reducing heat to finish cooking toward a 125°F center, a five-minute rest, and finishing with coarse salt for texture. The video also outlines the advantages and downsides of each method and notes how sous-vide and reverse-sear compare in precision and equipment needs.
topics: comparison with traditional sear + oven finish
comparison with sous-vide (gentle cook then quick sear)
kitchen equipment requirements (no special equipment for cold-sear)

sections.title: Traditional high-heat pan-sear (restaurant method)
sections.description: Lan Lam describes a classic sear: preheat a skillet until smoking, add oil, sear the steak, flip once, then finish in the oven to bring the center up to serving temperature. While this yields a strong crust, it risks a gray ring around a rosy center if overcooked and uses an oven finish for even doneness.

sections.title: Sous vide overview and trade-offs
sections.description: A concise primer on sous vide: vacuum-seal and water-bath cooking to fix internal temperature, followed by a quick sear. Drawbacks include cost of equipment, plastic bags, counter space, and longer total time relative to quick pan-sears.

sections.title: Reverse-sear method (Cook’s Illustrated origin)
concepts: temperature monitoring during both oven and sear
sections.description: The reverse-sear cooks the steak gently in a low oven to the near-final temperature, then finishes with a hot sear, combining crust development with precise doneness without relying on sous vide equipment.

sections.title: Cold-sear: dry, fast finish in a non-stick skillet
concepts: fat rendering and browning in its own fat
reduce heat to medium for even cooking
avoid gray band by heat management
sections.description: The centerpiece technique demonstrates a 1.5 inch thick steak seared dry in a preheated non-stick pan, without added oil. The surface is patted dry, peppered, and salt is saved for finishing. The steak is seared aggressively to drive off moisture, then flipped every two minutes while heat is adjusted to build a layered crust and cook toward a rosy center. A thermometer is used to confirm doneness around 125°F, followed by a five-minute rest and a coarse salt finish to add texture and flavor.
